A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting evaluations, component and head ablations, residual-stream measurements, and induction-head experiments, including results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds Chronos 2 evaluations, ablations, and forecast examples, notably in Appendix C.5.

M1.justification: The zero-ablation procedure, stable-rank head ordering, heads@1pp criterion, and direct logit attribution remain unchanged. The added Chronos 2 experiments apply the existing procedures to another model.

E1.justification: Both versions use GIFT-Eval and dysts, covering real-world forecasting, multivariate forecasts, and chaotic systems. Chronos 2 is evaluated within this retained coverage; no additional dataset or task domain is introduced.

E2.justification: Chronos 2 and its unablated reference are added to the evaluated ablation comparisons (Figure 3 and Tables 1 and 4). Existing model comparisons and random-head pruning comparisons remain; newly discussed pruning papers are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The new Chronos 2 experiments use an 8192-point context, patch length 16, nine forecast quantiles, and enabled cross-learning (Appendix A and Table 3). Existing models' settings, metrics, context sampling, and first-64-point Spearman evaluation are retained.

E4.justification: v2 extends layer/head sensitivity, forecast-preservation, and per-dataset analyses to Chronos 2 (Figures 17, 21, and 23; Table 5). Figure 27 adds another residual-stream case study. These are focused extensions of existing analyses; earlier ablations and induction-head investigations remain.

E5.justification: No new seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests are introduced. Additional plots continue existing variability-display conventions; forecast quantiles remain predictive outputs rather than a new experimental uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: New Chronos 2 results report 4.71% MASE and 3.92% CRPS increases after ablating 24% of heads and two MLPs, with 36 resilient and 24 improved splits (Tables 1 and 4). Table 5 and new figures add detailed results. Existing entries in Tables 1 and 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The kernel derivation, Proposition 4.1, its proof, and existing metric definitions are unchanged. However, new Appendix A.1 adds a non-equivalent residual recurrence: its final line adds the MLP output to H^(l), omitting the direct attention residual retained in Section 2.2. This introduces a limited mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about intermediate-layer redundancy, intrinsic pruning, and mechanisms underlying parroting and seasonality. Chronos 2 supplies additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A extends the GIFT-Eval pretraining-overlap qualification to Chronos 2. The Moirai dataset-dominance caveat gains prominence in Section 6 but already appeared in v1's Figure 19 caption. Other mechanism interpretations and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies Chronos 2 checkpoint identification, parameter and layer/head counts, and inference settings. Appendix A.3 also adds explicit default-versus-used configuration examples. The main code-access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused discussion of Wilinski, Zhao, and Pandey and their TSFM interpretability/pruning work, plus Tsai on attention kernels and Anagnostidis on rank collapse. These additions refine positioning within the existing research framing; the Dong reference update concerns the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 6, explanatory Appendix A.1 and Appendix B, and focused related-work expansions. It also corrects cross-references and wording and updates publication-header information. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Targeted additions include Chronos 2 displays, Table 5, expanded existing tables, and the Figure 27 example. Figure 8 redisplays the layer-4 results also shown in Figure 21. Existing figures largely retain their design, with local resizing, relocation, and reflow.

improvement.justification: The Chronos 2 analyses extend empirical support beyond v1's five-model study, while configuration details and closer engagement with related work improve reproducibility and positioning. These are limited gains because the central evidence and conclusions were already present. The new Appendix A.1 residual-update inconsistency is a localized drawback that does not outweigh those benefits.
